title: One gift. Two different purposes.
description: Client gifts and employee gifts need different briefs. Occasion, practical use and personalisation set the direction.

body.html: Client gifts and employee gifts need different briefs. Occasion, practical use and personalisation set the direction.

media.alt: Cognac luggage tag and burgundy keyring with an open presentation box.

blocks.html: A gift for an event guest can extend the occasion. An employee gift may mark joining the company, an anniversary or a shared achievement. Both need a clear connection to the recipient. A luggage tag used on business trips serves a different purpose from a desk pad at a permanent workstation. Choose the use first, then the accessory.

Bespoke leather luggage tags were used as giveaways at BMW Group Classic Events. SFP realised the accessories with Metzler+Vater. Their connection to travel gives the choice a clear rationale. For your own project, ask three questions: when will the gift be presented, how will it be used afterwards, and how visible should the branding be?

chapters.title: Employee gifts: connect daily use and occasion

blocks.html: Desk accessories may suit an onboarding set, while a personal travel accessory may suit a company anniversary. Decide whether everyone will receive the same set or whether different roles need different items. Where requested, names, initials and packaging should enter the discussion early. We assess the technical execution for the particular accessory.

A gift alone does not establish improved client retention or reduced staff turnover. Define a practical goal: a personal presentation, useful equipment or a well-considered occasion. Recipient feedback helps refine the selection for the next opportunity. To plan the project, we need the audience, quantity, presentation date and intended brand expression.

prose.summary: Planning a project of your own? Tell us the application, quantity and your idea. We’ll discuss the right specification with you.
